about.body:
Cybersecurity MSc graduate
awarded the NCR Atleos Prize for Best Student of the Programme.

Focused on Digital Forensics, Security Engineering and Secure Software Development.

Bridging offensive security and defensive engineering, from penetration testing to secure system architecture.

Security and privacy are part of the process from the very beginning.
about.remark: Currently available for freelance engagements and open to employment opportunities.

keys.title: Focus Areas
keys.services: Skills include, but are not limited to:

project-1.title: Mobile & Computer Forensics Case Studies (Academic Lab)
project-1.summary: Conducted two structured digital forensic investigations involving large-scale mobile device datasets (~60 extracted images including cloud and social media data) and a separate disk image analysis. Performed evidence triage, artifact analysis, timeline reconstruction and cross-source correlation under time constraints, with findings documented in detailed forensic reports.
general: Analysed large-scale mobile device datasets and a separate disk image using forensic investigation methodologies
Performed artifact extraction, keyword searches, file system analysis and registry/system artifact examination
Correlated findings across multiple evidence sources to reconstruct user activity and event timelines
Applied a hypothesis-driven and evidence-based investigation approach with clear separation of facts and interpretation
Produced structured forensic reports including evidence inventories, examination procedures, timeline reconstructions and substantiated findings
specific: Conducted structured forensic investigations across mobile, cloud/social media and disk image data
Performed artifact identification, file system and registry analysis, keyword searching and timeline reconstruction
Documented forensic findings in clear, structured and evidence-based reports
Triaged and prioritised relevant evidence under time constraints
Analysed and correlated forensic findings to support investigative and response decision-making
Supported post-incident analysis, containment and remediation planning through forensic investigations

project-2.title: Digital Forensics Case Management Framework & Tool Prototype (Master Thesis)
project-2.summary: Researched digital forensics case management practices and developed a requirements framework for forensic case management systems. Based on this framework and a gap analysis of existing tools, designed and prototyped a secure, forensically sound digital forensics case management system with a focus on evidence integrity, chain of custody, security-by-design and investigator workflows.
project-2.remark: Currently being written up as a paper.
general: Conducted academic research on digital forensics case management and derived a structured requirements framework
Compared existing forensic case management tools against the framework to identify capability and workflow gaps
Designed a comprehensive DF case management system focused on forensic soundness, secure evidence handling, usability and structured workflows
Defined system architecture with microservices, trust boundaries, role-based access control, audit logging and integrity protection mechanisms
Implemented a proof-of-concept prototype using FastAPI, Python, React, PostgreSQL, Docker Compose and Keycloak
specific: Gained strong understanding of forensic case management workflows, chain of custody requirements and evidence integrity principles
Translated forensic best practices and investigative requirements into structured workflows and system design decisions
Gained understanding of how secure case management and evidence handling support efficient DFIR investigations and triage processes
Designed and partially built a full-stack microservices prototype using FastAPI, React, PostgreSQL, Docker and Keycloak
Applied security-by-design principles including trust zones, access control, audit logging and cryptographic integrity protections
Translated complex research and domain requirements into scalable system architecture and prototype implementations

project-3.title: Forensic Artifact Processing Automation Tool (Open Source)
project-3.summary: Designed and developed a platform-independent CLI tool in Python to automate forensic artifact processing workflows. The Docker-based application parses Foremost outputs, extracts and normalises metadata using ExifTool, detects duplicate files, stores results in a database and generates structured JSON reports to support efficient forensic analysis and triage.
project-3.remark: Open-source beta release available on GitHub.
general: Developed a platform-independent CLI application in Python for forensic artifact processing and reporting
Parsed Foremost file carving outputs and extracted structured artifact information
Integrated ExifTool to collect and normalise metadata from recovered files and implemented duplicate detection
Stored processed artifact data in a PostgreSQL database and generated structured JSON reports
Built a Docker-based cross-platform solution with Bash and PowerShell startup scripts, input validation and error handling
specific: Worked with file carving outputs, forensic artifacts and metadata analysis workflows
Gained understanding of how automation supports efficient forensic triage and evidence review processes
Structured forensic data and reports to support investigation and analysis workflows
Built containerised Python CLI application using Docker and PostgreSQL
Designed data processing pipeline including parsing, metadata extraction, deduplication and reporting
Applied software engineering practices including modular design, error handling, input validation and cross-platform scripting with Bash and PowerShell

project-4.title: Manual Open-Source Web Application Security Assessment (Real-World)
project-4.summary: Conducted a full manual security assessment of a zero-knowledge open-source web application in a local VM environment. Performed a manual security assessment of a zero-knowledge open-source web application in a local VM environment. Identified security flaws, business logic issues and social engineering risks through code review, traffic analysis and browser-based testing.
general: Set up and tested a zero-knowledge open-source web application in a local VM environment
Performed basic code review and analysed application behaviour through browser/UI testing
Used Burp Suite for network traffic analysis, request manipulation and attack validation
Tested for XSS, CSRF, business logic flaws, validation weaknesses and client-side bypasses
Identified security bugs and social engineering/phishing possibilities, then documented and disclosed findings responsibly
specific: Improved manual web application testing skills beyond automated vulnerability scanning
Gained hands-on experience with Burp Suite, browser analysis, request manipulation and exploit validation
Learned how business logic flaws and social engineering opportunities can create realistic attack paths
Developed a stronger understanding of secure validation, trust boundaries and client–server security design
Learned how weak input validation and client-side controls can lead to exploitable security gaps
Improved vulnerability classification, reporting and communication with developers during responsible disclosure processes

project-5.title: Windows Domain Security Assessment (Academic Lab)
project-5.summary: Performed a hands-on penetration test against a Windows Active Directory lab environment simulating common enterprise weaknesses. Identified and exploited misconfigurations leading to credential compromise, privilege escalation and system-level access.
general: Performed network and service enumeration with Nmap across SMB, DNS, SMTP, FTP, RDP and SSH
Used Nessus and manual validation to identify vulnerabilities and exposed services
Analysed Active Directory users, authentication mechanisms, password policies and service configurations
Exploited misconfigurations for credential harvesting, password cracking, privilege escalation and admin account compromise
Gained system-level access on a target server and documented attack paths and remediation recommendations
specific: Improved practical Active Directory pentesting skills from enumeration to full system compromise
Gained hands-on experience with Nmap, Nessus, credential attacks and privilege escalation techniques
Learned how multiple small weaknesses can be chained into realistic enterprise attack paths
Developed a stronger understanding of common Windows AD misconfigurations and hardening practices
Learned how weak authentication, permissions and exposed services increase enterprise attack surface
Improved technical reporting, root cause analysis and remediation recommendation skills

project-6.title: OWASP-based Web Application Pentest (Academic Lab)
project-6.summary: Performed a methodology-driven web application penetration test based on the OWASP Testing Guide, combining automated scanning with manual validation and exploitation. Identified and demonstrated vulnerabilities including SQL injection, XSS, broken authentication, session hijacking and business logic flaws in a realistic attack scenario.
general: Conducted reconnaissance and attack surface mapping against the target web application
Tested authentication, authorisation, session management, input validation and business logic
Used OWASP ZAP, Wapiti, and Nessus to identify vulnerabilities and manually validate findings

Exploited SQL injection for database access using manual techniques and sqlmap, leveraged XSS with BeEF hook for client-side control, used Weevely for post-exploitation activities and demonstrated admin session replay attacks
Documented confirmed findings, exploitation evidence, attack paths and mitigation recommendations in a structured report
specific: Improved practical web application pentesting skills using the OWASP Testing Guide as a structured methodology
Gained hands-on experience exploiting SQLi, XSS, broken authentication, session hijacking and business logic vulnerabilities
Learned how to validate automated scan results manually and chain vulnerabilities into realistic attack scenarios

project-7.title: Linux Home Server
project-7.summary: Deployed and maintained a self-hosted Linux server on a Raspberry Pi providing Nextcloud, SMB file sharing and VPN access. Secured and administered the system entirely via CLI using Linux hardening practices, firewall configuration, system monitoring and OpenVPN integration.
general: Deployed and configured Nextcloud for remote file access and SMB for local network file sharing and backups
Secured the system using firewall configuration and Linux hardening practices
Performed ongoing maintenance including system updates, log analysis, process inspection and basic network traffic review
Reconfigured the Raspberry Pi into a media system while maintaining system hardening and adding OpenVPN for access protection
Managed the entire environment through CLI/Bash administration and documented all setup and configuration steps for reproducibility
specific: Gained practical experience hardening Linux systems and reducing attack surface on a self-hosted environment
Learned secure access configuration and VPN deployment with OpenVPN
Improved operational security skills through continuous maintenance, monitoring, troubleshooting and log analysis
Strengthened Linux system administration and command-line workflow skills through daily hands-on use
Gained experience deploying, configuring and maintaining self-hosted infrastructure and network services
Developed structured troubleshooting and technical documentation practices for reproducible system setups

project-8.title: Cryptanalysis of DiCal-IDEA implementation (Bachelor Thesis)
project-8.summary: Conducted a structured analysis of the DiCal-IDEA encryption used in the POCSAG protocol for BOS paging systems. Analysed 236 ciphertext samples, protocol metadata and public resources to identify likely message structures, encryption methods and IV handling through ciphertext-only and hypothesis-driven analysis, followed by threat modelling of potential weaknesses and attack vectors.
general: Researched existing cryptanalysis and technical documentation related to the IDEA cipher and DiCal-IDEA implementations
Analysed encrypted POCSAG message datasets and correlated ciphertext patterns with protocol metadata and timestamps
Developed and tested multiple hypotheses regarding message structure, cipher mode operation, IV usage and nonce construction
Applied exclusion-based analytical methods to identify technically plausible encryption implementations
Produced a threat modelling assessment of the identified and hypothesised cryptographic design choices
specific: Analysed proprietary cryptographic implementations with limited technical information
Identified potential attack vectors and weaknesses through threat modelling and protocol analysis
Improved hypothesis-driven security analysis and technical validation methodologies
Conducted structured investigations on encrypted communication datasets
Performed metadata correlation, protocol artifact analysis and timeline-based investigation methods
Documented technical findings in clear, structured and evidence-based analytical reports

experience-1.title: Cybersecurity Student Assistant (Part-Time)
experience-1.summary: Designed and secured a structured penetration testing training environment with hands-on attack labs and realistic security scenarios. Built clear exercise documentation, assessment procedures and operational security controls to support safe and repeatable training.
general: Designed a penetration testing lab with realistic attack scenarios and hands-on exercises
Created structured training documentation and methodology-based exercise materials
Secured the lab environment with access controls, firewall rules and restricted permissions
Established a responsible disclosure workflow and defined operational boundaries
specific: Improved practical understanding of penetration testing methodologies and attack workflows
Learned how to design realistic offensive security scenarios for hands-on training environments
Gained experience defining responsible disclosure processes and engagement boundaries
Applied infrastructure hardening through firewall configuration and access control management
Learned how to secure isolated training environments while maintaining usability
Improved understanding of trust boundaries, permission scoping and operational security controls

experience-2.title: Data Privacy & Security Intern (Full-time)
experience-2.summary: Completed a data protection and security internship focused on GDPR compliance, European data privacy law research and web application security assessments. Analysed PII processing risks, performed scoped vulnerability testing and worked with administrators to improve security and compliance.
general: Conducted detailed research on European data privacy laws, GDPR requirements and fundamental legal case analysis
Analysed university data flows and data protection requirements in a GDPR context
Created RoPA documentation and supported compliance-related processes
Assessed university web applications to identify PII processing points and related risks
Performed scoped vulnerability assessments with structured triage and prioritisation while collaborating with administrators on mitigation efforts
specific: Developed a practical understanding of GDPR requirements, RoPA creation and PII classification in institutional environments
Learned how to analyse data processing activities using structured legal reasoning and statutory element analysis
Improved understanding of how data privacy regulations apply to real technical systems and workflows
Gained experience performing scoped web application vulnerability assessments and structured finding triage
Learned how privacy risks and technical security vulnerabilities overlap in web applications handling sensitive data
Improved communication and remediation coordination skills by working directly with system administrators and stakeholders

experience-3.title: Software Developer - Forensic Lab Equipment (Part-time)
experience-3.summary: Independently refactored and extended a legacy C# desktop application used for forensic lab equipment log processing. Improved code structure, redesigned GUI-based data visualisation and rebuilt documentation while collaborating with hardware and sales stakeholders.
general: Independently refactored and extended a legacy C# Windows desktop application used for forensic log processing
Restructured existing code and applied design patterns to improve maintainability, readability and data handling
Redesigned the GUI-based log visualisation to make data easier to analyse and report
Rebuilt technical documentation to reflect the updated system architecture and workflows
Collaborated with hardware and sales stakeholders to ensure accurate data representation and user-friendly output while managing version control with SVN
specific: Gained hands-on experience working with and improving a legacy C# codebase independently
Strengthened understanding of refactoring, software architecture and design patterns in a real production environment
Improved communication skills by translating technical requirements into practical features and clear user-facing functionality

education-1.title: Master of Science in Ethical Hacking & Cybersecurity
education-1.prize: NCR Atleos Prize for Best Student of the Programme
education-1.summary: Completed a Master's degree covering advanced cybersecurity topics including digital forensics, penetration testing, network security, basic malware analysis and incident response, basic information security governance and data privacy law.
education-1.thesis: The master's thesis focused on designing a Digital Forensics Case Management Framework and Tool Prototype, optimising workflows, evidence handling and usability.

education-2.title: Bachelor of Science in Applied Computer Science
education-2.grades: Graduated 1.7 - Equivalent to UK Upper Second Class Honours (2:1)
education-2.summary: Completed a Bachelor's degree building a broad foundation across software development, networking, system administration, databases, with lectures on AI, mobile forensics and European data privacy law.
education-2.thesis: The bachelor's thesis involved a cryptographic analysis of a proprietary IDEA implementation.

PT: Manual Open-Source Web Application Security Assessment

certificate-1.title: CCNA Routing and Switching: Introduction to Networks
certificate-1.summary: Completed the Cisco CCNA Routing & Switching: Introduction to Networks course with hands-on networking labs using Cisco hardware and Packet Tracer. Learned core networking fundamentals including TCP/IP, subnetting, switching, routing, VLANs and WAN concepts while configuring and troubleshooting real network setups.
general: Studied core networking concepts including TCP/IP, the OSI model, subnetting, VLANs, switching and routing fundamentals
Configured Cisco routers and switches through the command line, including IP addressing, device setup and basic network management
Built and troubleshot small-to-medium network topologies using physical hardware, incl. Windows PCs, and Cisco Packet Tracer
Worked with routing concepts, WAN connectivity, wireless networking and hardware-level data transmission
Practiced identifying and resolving network connectivity issues in structured lab environments
specific: Built a strong understanding of how computer networks function across infrastructure, devices, and internet communication
Gained practical experience configuring and troubleshooting Cisco networking equipment in hands-on lab environments
Learned to analyse network problems systematically using subnetting, routing logic and connectivity testing

reference-1.body: I have known Blue since his enrolment on the MSc Ethical Hacking programme at Abertay in September 2024, when he took my Digital Forensics class. Blue quickly stood out as an exceptionally capable student, bringing intelligence, diligence and thoroughness to every task. His approach to complex problems was mature, methodical and determined, underpinned by a genuine enthusiasm for the subject. It was therefore no surprise when Blue was awarded the NCR Atleos Prize for Best Student on the Programme. Beyond his academic strengths, Blue is thoughtful, reliable, engaging and easy to work with: a real asset to any team.

reference-2.body: Blue consistently demonstrated reliability and professionalism. He was punctual, arrived prepared and ready to begin work. His self-directed approach meant he took initiative, managed tasks independently, and required minimal supervision. Blue also showed strong discipline and maintained steady progress on all assigned work. Overall, it was encouraging to see his commitment to producing quality work.

values.subtitle: This page explains if, how and by whom personal data is processed.
values.website:
This website does not collect, store or process any personal data of visitors. This website does not use cookies or any form of tracking (incl. Google Analytics).

This website may contain links to third-party services such as LinkedIn or GitHub. When visiting those external websites, personal data and technical information, such as IP addresses, browser information or request data, may be automatically processed by the respective providers.

Please refer to their respective privacy policies for more details.
